Duration::to_note_iso¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Note Duration::to_note_iso() const;

ISO Duration Projection¶

to_note_iso() converts each elapsed value to ISO duration text: P starts the duration, D carries whole days, T introduces time fields, and H, M, and S label those fields. Zero is PT0S; a negative duration has one leading minus sign, such as -PT0.000000001S.

Zero-valued fields are omitted unless needed to express zero itself. Fractional seconds retain every significant nanosecond digit and discard only trailing zeros. The conversion is lossless for finite Duration lanes at nanosecond precision. NaT is emitted as "NaT", since absence is not an ISO duration.

The result is an owning UTF-8 Note with the same shape and lane order as the receiver. This method differs semantically from to_note(); it is not an alias for the fixed-field display form.

Examples¶

Example 1. Composite, negative, zero, and absent values.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {93'784'005'006'007LL, -1, 0, pluss::Duration::kNaT});
std::cout << values.to_note_iso();

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["P1DT2H3M4.005006007S", "-PT0.000000001S", "PT0S", "NaT"]

Example 2. Exact whole units omit redundant fields.

auto matrix = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {0, -1, 1'000'000'000, 86'400'000'000'000LL}, {2,2});
std::cout << matrix.to_note_iso();

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["PT0S", "-PT0.000000001S"],
  ["PT1S", "P1D"]
]

Example 3. Fractional precision contracts only on the right.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos({1'500'000'000, 1'000'000'001});
auto text = values.to_note_iso(); // ["PT1.5S", "PT1.000000001S"]
